calmeddy_thinning.png.description: Thinning rate of the floe's (single, area-mean) thickness in cm/day against time, one panel per floe radius (1, 2, 4, 8 km). Black: paper's constant q. Blue: dynamic heat transfer, u*_min = 0.0005 m/s. Orange dashed: dynamic, u*_min = 0.002 m/s. calmeddy_cummelt.png.title: Cumulative melt in each grid cell under the floe, shared colour scale (calm)
calmeddy_cummelt.png.description: Total melt over the run in each grid cell under the floe (cm), from the exact running sum saved by the driver (melt_cum), divided by the cell's ice cover so that partly covered rim cells show the local thinning. Columns: floe radius 1, 2, 4, 8 km. Rows: constant q, dynamic u*_min = 0.0005, dynamic u*_min = 0.002. ONE colour scale for all panels (colour bar on the right column), so amounts can be compared between panels. Panel titles give the floe-mean melt. Diagnostic only: the model thins each floe uniformly; the map shows where the heat was delivered.

calmeddy_cummelt_pattern.png.title: Pattern of cumulative melt under the floe, deviation from the floe mean in cm (calm)

Panel titles give the floe mean and the range of deviations. Each panel has its own symmetric colour scale, so the pattern inside each floe is visible; amounts are compared in calmeddy_cummelt.png. Constant-q floes are uniform (differences are rounding only). In dynamic runs, rings of high melt mark radii where the rigidly rotating floe and the eddy water move at different speeds; low-melt centre and rings mark where they match.

tiltcheck.png.title: Tilt / drag check: floe tracks and distance from the eddy centre
tiltcheck.png.description: Anticyclonic eddy (radius 4 km, 0.08 m/s; background: vorticity ζ/f, blue = anticyclonic), one 2 km floe, melting off, 5 days. Left: calm, floe starting 4 km from the eddy centre. Right: steady 3 m/s wind towards +x, floe starting at the centre. Red: original module (component-wise drag), no tilt. Blue: vector drag (Eq. 2), no tilt. Green: vector drag + sea-surface tilt (gradient-wind balance). Top: tracks (circles: floe at the end). Bottom: distance of the floe centre from the eddy centre; decreasing = drawn in (retained), increasing = escaping.
